claims.text: As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has room-temperature tensile ductility of 8–16%.
As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a high-temperature yield strength of 163–530 MPa.
Untreated HfNbTaTiZr has inadequate oxidation resistance for high-temperature use in oxygen-containing atmospheres.
Untreated HfNbTaTiZr undergoes rapid oxidation in oxygen-rich high-temperature environments.
A nanoscale conformal Al2O3 coating can be deposited on as-cast HfNbTaTiZr by atomic layer deposition.
An anti-oxidation coating is a relevant intervention for enabling high-temperature use of this alloy system in air.
The ALD-deposited Al2O3 layer will impede oxygen diffusion into HfNbTaTiZr.
Al2O3 will remain a stable protective barrier at approximately 1000 °C in an oxygen-rich atmosphere.
Reduced oxygen ingress will suppress oxidation and oxygen-induced embrittlement of the underlying alloy.
Suppressing oxygen ingress will preserve the underlying alloy microstructure.
The coated alloy will exhibit less oxide-scale formation, oxidation mass gain, or oxidation depth than an untreated control after 100 hours at approximately 1000 °C.
The coating will preserve the alloy's room-temperature tensile ductility.
The coating will preserve the alloy's high-temperature yield strength under strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1.
The proposed protective effect applies for oxygen-rich exposure at approximately 1000 °C for up to about 100 hours and mechanical strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1.

contradictions.description: The conditions specify mechanical testing concurrent with the 1000 °C oxygen exposure, whereas the experiment specifies tensile testing following the exposure.

The hypothesis and measurements distinguish room-temperature ductility from high-temperature yield strength, but the predicted outcome ambiguously states that both established ductility and yield strength will be maintained at high temperatures.
